name: Menelaion
text: The Menelaion (Ancient Greek: Μενελάειον, romanized: Menelaeion) is an archaeological site in Therapne (Laconia, Greece), located on a ridge approximately 5 km from the modern (and classical) city of Sparta. The archaeological hill complex of Therapne dates from the Bronze Age Mycenaean civilization and comprises four hills: the Northern hill, Menelaion, Profitis Ilias and Aetos. The archaic name of the place was also Therapne (Ancient Greek: Θεράπνη).

depictions.name: Menelaion
depictions.text: The Menelaion was a shrine located on a rocky cliff overlooking the city of Sparta in Lakonia. It was dedicated to King Menelaus of Sparta and his wife Helen. During the Peloponnesian War the sanctuary was visited by the Spartan misthios Kassandra.
